Hi all,

Quick answers from the platform side after a quick review: 

1) 7-day active purge SLA
- Feasible for hosted customers in the common-case. Our active deletion pipeline will mark the tenant objects for deletion and asynchronously remove them from primary stores. Typical observed completion is <48 hours; 7 days provides a safe buffer for queued jobs/edge cases. For Dedicated/private installs we need to confirm customer-managed backup policies separately.

2) Backups and restores
- Current behavior: backups are incremental snapshots kept for configured retention windows (default 30 days, configurable up to 90). We do not automatically scrub deleted records from existing immutable snapshots. However, we have two mitigations:
  a) Restore-time filtering: our restore process supports tenant-level include/exclude filters. When restoring a snapshot, ops can exclude specified tenant ids so deleted data is not reintroduced.
  b) Snapshot TTL: for hosted customers we can schedule expedited snapshot expiry for specific tenants (subject to storage and retention policy constraints). This is typically 30-45 days to fully reach snapshots taken after deletion.

Operational implications: If FinTechCo requires guaranteed zero possibility of reintroduction from backups before 45 days, we recommend combining a 7-day active purge with an expedited snapshot expiry policy and a restore exclusion policy.

3) Audit / attestation
- We can produce an exportable CSV/JSON with the following fields: request_id, tenant_id, object_type, object_id_list (comma-separated), deletion_step (active|index|backup-mark), timestamp_utc, operator (automation|manual), job_id.
- Example: request_id=RTBF-FT-00073, tenant_id=fintechco-prod, object_type=embedding_index, object_id_list=vec-12345, deletion_step=index, timestamp_utc=2026-03-06T09:00:12Z, operator=automation, job_id=job-8891

Attachments: I'm attaching a short SOC2_evidence_summary.xlsx with pointers to relevant controls (access logs, deletion runbooks).

Happy to join the call tomorrow to walk through the MOP. If Jordan wants stricter timelines on snapshot expiry we can scope an implementation plan and run it by Product.

Thanks,
